themes.label: Wrist-first battleground: top-roll vs wrist control and flop press
themes.why_this_theme_emerged: Multiple claims emphasize Ermes Gasparini’s toproll approach and the need to force or defend the opponent’s wrist, with references to plan B flop presses when wrists are compromised. The Morozov side is framed around capable wrist control and hand-cup, suggesting the match may hinge on who can control or crack the other's wrist first.
themes.match_relevance: Critical because the right-hand match hinges on a wrist-cup battle and the viability of finishing moves (flop press) once a wrist is compromised. If Morozov can cinch Ermes’s wrist, his height/frame pressure becomes decisive; if Ermes can keep the wrist neutralized, his back-pressure and flop-press transitions become the path to victory.
